articles.originalTitle: angelo renna’s eight principles for welcoming non-human life back into our cities - Designboom
articles.title: Eight Principles for Welcoming Non-Human Life into Urban Design
articles.excerpt: Designer Angelo Renna has published an eight-principle guide for integrating non-human species into urban environments. The recommendations focus on allowing spontaneous green growth, reducing lawn maintenance, and incorporating natural habitats.
articles.content: As human activities over the past half-century have contributed to a significant decline in global wildlife populations, designer Angelo Renna has outlined an eight-principle framework for integrating non-human species into urban environments. The guidelines advocate for allowing urban ecosystems to emerge naturally without excessive landscaping control, alongside reducing the frequency of intensive lawn mowing, which research links to decreased plant and invertebrate diversity. Additional principles include incorporating decaying tree trunks and snags to provide food and shelter for various organisms, providing water sources beyond simple drinking facilities for amphibians and insects, and utilizing porous construction materials and dry-stacked bricks to form microhabitats. The framework also emphasizes choosing diverse multispecies vegetation communities over monocultures to increase ecological resilience against environmental stress. Ultimately, the proposals envision the future city not merely as a human-centric development process, but as a shared habitat characterized by interspecific co-evolution and coexistence between humans and other forms of life.

articles.originalTitle: ‘Strain and Resilience’: Alma Allen at Perrotin Paris - ArtReview
articles.title: Alma Allen Presents First Solo Exhibition at Perrotin Paris
articles.excerpt: Perrotin is hosting Alma Allen's first solo exhibition featuring monumental bronze sculptures at its Paris space through December 19, exploring touch, memory, and perception.
articles.content: Perrotin is presenting Alma Allen's first solo exhibition with the gallery, bringing a new body of monumental bronze sculptures to its Paris space. On view from October 17 through December 19, the exhibition introduces works that explore touch, transformation, memory, and perception. Each sculpture is titled Not Yet Titled, reflecting the artist's belief that meaning should remain open. Their surfaces and contours suggest roots, seed pods, fossils, and shells while resisting single classification. Beginning on an intimate scale with string, clay, or wax, the self-taught sculptor develops small models by hand, a practice originating from his teenage years in Utah. The small models are subsequently scanned, enlarged, and cast in bronze at the artist's home foundry. The resulting sculptures communicate both strain and resilience, recalling nautical knots and ropes pulled through water. Several pieces were developed aboard his boat following time spent in Venice. Alongside freestanding sculptures, the exhibition features bronze wall reliefs bearing surfaces kneaded by hand. The polished patinas of the bronzes are intended to evolve over time, echoing stone weathering. The new works occupy the space between the physical and the mysterious at Perrotin Paris.

articles.originalTitle: Van Gogh painting sells for record $190m at Sotheby’s following Nazi loot claims - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Van Gogh painting achieves record 190.4 million dollars at New York auction
articles.excerpt: One of Vincent van Gogh's final paintings sold for 190.4 million dollars with fees at Sotheby's, breaking the artist's auction record following a settlement regarding Nazi-era provenance claims.
articles.content: Vincent van Gogh's 1890 painting Blossoming Chestnut Trees sold for 165 million dollars, totaling 190.4 million dollars with fees, at Sotheby's New York, breaking the artist's previous auction record. Long kept out of public view in the Blaquier-Arrieta collection, the artwork went to a room bidder after nearly five minutes of competition. Just a day before the event, Sotheby's announced a settlement between the Blaquier heirs and the heirs of previous owners Hedwig and Samuel Fischer regarding Nazi-era provenance questions. The result makes the painting the second most valuable object ever sold at Sotheby's and the fourth most valuable painting at auction. Back-to-back New York sales generated a combined 777.8 million dollars with fees. Additional auction records were set by Mary Cassatt and Aaron Douglas. Douglas's Harriet Tubman hammered at 12 million dollars, reaching 14.48 million dollars with fees, with proceeds to benefit Bennett College. Cassatt's Summertime fetched 13.3 million dollars with fees, surpassing its estimate. Six lots from the Blaquier-Arrieta collection hammered below low estimates, while the Modern Evening sale achieved 365.8 million dollars with fees amid patchy bidding.

articles.originalTitle: About the Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires exhibition - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Constantinople to Istanbul Exhibition Explores Sixteen Centuries of Art at V&A
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum presents Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires, an exhibition featuring over 200 objects that explore 1,600 years of artistic production across the Byzantine and Ottoman empires.
articles.content: The Victoria and Albert Museum is hosting a comprehensive exhibition titled Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires, which runs until 9 May 2027. The exhibition explores 1,600 years of artistic production spanning from AD 330 to 1922. It examines the enduring creative legacy of an imperial capital that shaped the Mediterranean world and beyond, highlighting the distinct yet connected traditions of both the Byzantine and Ottoman empires. The display showcases more than 200 objects across four main sections, featuring rare decorative arts, fine silks, ceramic tiles, mosaics, precious metalwork, jewellery, sculptures, manuscripts, and paintings. The exhibition is organized into four thematic sections: Roman Beginnings, Heaven and Earth, Power and Reach, and Life in the City. The opening section covers the refounding of the city in AD 330 as the capital of the Roman Empire, followed by sections exploring sacred imagery in Christianity, the visual spectacle of Ottoman court authority, and the cosmopolitan rhythms of urban life characterized by diverse languages and faiths. The exhibition concludes by tracing the influence of Byzantine and Ottoman art on 19th-century European culture.

articles.content: Bjarke Ingels Group has revealed plans for Nachwachsende Stadt, a new 13,000-square-meter timber development located in Thun, Switzerland. Selected through a competition organized by Frutiger AG and the city of Thun, the scheme includes two hotels and residential buildings featuring stacked wooden volumes and deep window grids. The development allocates approximately 6,500 square meters for residential uses, 6,000 square meters for hotels, and 400 square meters for commercial activities. At the southwest corner, a combined three-star and four-star hotel structure features shared amenity spaces, outdoor terraces, and a rooftop restaurant. The eastern residential buildings frame a shared garden courtyard with flexible apartment layouts and private balconies. Sustainability measures also include green roofs, rainwater retention systems, and approximately 1,800 square meters of photovoltaic panels. The development is targeting Switzerland's SNBS Gold certification, with construction on the first buildings possible starting in 2028.

articles.originalTitle: Mary Miss’s Long Fight to Keep Public Art Alive - ARTnews.com
articles.title: Mary Miss and Her Long Career Shaping the Boundaries of Public Art
articles.excerpt: Pioneering public artist Mary Miss reflects on decades of creating site-specific works that challenge conventional definitions of art, architecture, and landscape in the modern world.
articles.content: Born in 1944, Mary Miss emerged as a pioneering figure in the public art revolution of the 1980s, moving away from static monuments toward participatory installations. Among her most celebrated works is South Cove, a waterside park created between 1984 and 1987 in Manhattan's Battery Park City, which integrated natural elements with maritime history. Throughout a career spanning decades, Miss encountered bureaucratic obstacles, budget limitations, nonpayment, and the dismantling of signature pieces. Rather than deterring her, these challenges prompted her to adapt her approach, culminating in ongoing community-focused initiatives such as her City as Living Laboratory project. From her early outdoor constructions in Colorado to urban interventions that incorporated deep site research, her practice consistently challenged conventional definitions of public art. Her 1977 installation Perimeters, Pavilions, Decoys notably helped shape critical discourse regarding sculpture in the expanded field, engaging directly with architecture and landscape. Despite shifts in public funding and political climates, Miss maintains a steadfast dedication to fostering connections and dialogue through art created specifically for public spaces.

articles.originalTitle: EU Countries Renew Call To Exclude Russia from Venice Ahead of 2027 Architecture Biennale - ARTnews.com
articles.title: Ten European Union nations demand exclusion of Russia from Venice Biennale

articles.content: Ten European Union nations, including Poland, Austria, Croatia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Germany, Latvia, Lithuania, and Sweden, demanded sustained efforts from the European Commission to exclude Russia from the 2027 Venice Architecture Biennial. According to a diplomatic note, Moscow's presence on the cultural stage risks normalizing its war on Ukraine while lacking a just and lasting peace. Russia previously returned to the Biennale in May following its 2022 invasion of Ukraine, drawing widespread condemnation from artists and politicians. The European Commission suspended a 2 million euro grant to the Biennale in July after urging organizers to exclude Moscow. Biennale president Pietrangelo Buttafuoco defended the inclusion, stating that the institution rejects the censorship of culture and art. The upcoming Architecture Biennial is scheduled to run from May 8 to November 21, 2027, under the curatorial theme Do Architecture led by Wang Shu and Lu Wenyu.

articles.originalTitle: Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires – exhibition large print guide - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Victoria and Albert Museum Publishes Constantinople Exhibition Guide
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum has published a comprehensive exhibition guide examining the rich history, art, and architecture of the city that served as capital to two empires.
articles.content: The Victoria and Albert Museum has issued an exhibition guide detailing the historical transformation from Constantinople to Istanbul. In 324 CE, Emperor Constantine I selected the ancient site as his new capital, naming it Nova Roma before it became known as Constantinople. The settlement served as the capital of the Byzantine Empire until 1453, and subsequently as the Ottoman capital until 1922. Situated at the junction of Asia and Europe, the metropolis flourished through trade, taxation, and loot, funding outstanding public works and architecture. The exhibition explores the city's vital engineering feats, including the 5.6-kilometer Theodosian Walls and the 4th-century Aqueduct of Valens. Religious life transitioned through Roman paganism, Christianity, and Islam, while a diverse population of merchants and craftspeople inhabited the urban center. The guide highlights various historical objects, such as ivory plaques of Christ Pantocrator, Hâfız Osman's calligraphy describing the Prophet Muhammad, restoration inscriptions of Emperor Michael III, and cameos made from rock crystal, lapis lazuli, and amethyst. These artifacts demonstrate the two distinct traditions of art and design practiced within the city across its long imperial history.

articles.originalTitle: 2026 Record Awards: Jules & Jim Bridges by Dietmar Feichtinger Architects - Architectural Record
articles.title: New Pedestrian Bridges Reconnect Historic Centers Across the Seine Near Paris
articles.excerpt: Designed by Dietmar Feichtinger Architectes, the Jules and Jim bridges restore a historic link destroyed in World War II, creating a continuous pedestrian and bicycle route connecting Mantes-la-Jolie and Limay.
articles.content: Constructed over the Seine River in France, a pair of pedestrian footbridges named Jules and Jim reconnect the historic centers of Mantes-la-Jolie and Limay. Located about 30 miles west of Paris, the project restores a link lost with the destruction of a medieval bridge during World War II. The design introduces two contemporary crossings, establishing a continuous pedestrian and bicycle route connecting public spaces, parks, and cultural landmarks. The 660-foot Jules bridge spans from Mantes to the Île aux Dames in the middle of the river, utilizing existing masonry piers of the adjacent vehicular crossing to minimize riverbed disruption. The 80-foot Jim bridge connects the island and Limay by spanning extant sections of the medieval crossing. Named after a 1962 film by François Truffaut, the project transforms a historical rupture into a renewed connection. The client for the initiative is the Syndicat Mixte d’aménagement, de gestion et d’entretien des berges de la Seine et Oise. Dietmar Feichtinger Architectes served as the architect, with engineering by Terrell SAS, historic monument consulting by ALEP Architectes, and lighting design by Coup d’éclat.

articles.title: Construction Progresses on Jean Nouvel's Opera House in China

articles.content: French architecture practice Ateliers Jean Nouvel has released photographs revealing ongoing construction progress on the massive Shenzhen Opera House in China. Slated for completion in 2028, the project is situated on the Shekou Peninsula overlooking Shenzhen Bay. Designed by Pritzker Prize-winning architect Jean Nouvel's studio, the 250,000-square-metre waterfront cultural landmark is defined by an elongated, wavy roofscape that reflects the site's coastal context. articles.originalTitle: Building a Permanent Home for a Space Shuttle Was an Engineering Endeavor - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: New Center for Space Shuttle Endeavour Completed in Los Angeles
articles.excerpt: The $450-million Samuel Oschin Air and Space Center at the California Science Center opened its doors. Retired space shuttle Endeavour is exhibited in launch position, marking a unique engineering endeavor.
articles.content: The 200,000-square-foot Samuel Oschin Air and Space Center at the California Science Center has been completed. Having flown its final mission in 2011, space shuttle Endeavour is exhibited in launch configuration alongside two solid rocket boosters and an external tank. ZGF Architects, MATT Construction, and engineering teams designed a 200-foot-tall stainless-steel structure around the shuttle geometry. Arup provided structural and civil engineering, applying performance-based seismic analysis and triple-friction pendulum isolator bearings to separate the foundation from ground movements during earthquakes. Shotcrete concrete was used for the lower facade for cost savings, while the upper portion features a structural steel diagrid designed with 3D software. Crews erected the diagrid using temporary shoring towers and maintained strict safety protocols for fragile silica tiles. The center was designed 25 feet below grade to prevent the tall hall from dwarfing nearby campus facilities.

articles.originalTitle: Eight Dead, 18 Injured in Brooklyn Building Collapse Next to Construction Site - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: Eight Dead and 18 Injured in Brooklyn Building Collapse Near Construction Site
articles.excerpt: An adjoining 96-year-old three-story building collapsed into an excavation site in Brooklyn, New York, leaving 8 people dead and 18 injured. Authorities have launched multiple investigations into the incident.
articles.content: On November 11, a three-story building collapsed into an adjoining excavation site in the Brooklyn borough of New York, resulting in 8 fatalities and 18 injuries. Officials confirmed the dead included two children and two construction workers, while the Fire Department concluded rescue operations on November 12. City records list Townhouse Builders as the general contractor for the project at 2625 Bedford Ave. A project geotechnical report had warned that abutting structures required underpinning and that construction-related vibrations could adversely affect neighboring properties. A March 5 preconstruction survey documented visible cracking at 1321 Flatbush Ave., rating its north masonry facade as poor and its other facades as fair. Area residents reported feeling heavy impacts and shaking while construction was underway next door. Mayor Zohran Mamdani ordered safety inspections at approximately 100 other construction sites linked to companies involved in the project. New York Attorney General Letitia James stated that the Buildings Department would conduct a full investigation, alongside a separate probe launched by Brooklyn District Attorney Eric Gonzalez. The exact cause of the structural collapse remains undetermined pending the conclusion of ongoing investigations by municipal authorities.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | TAREK EL-ARISS | Emptying the Jars of War, or How We Learned to Love Nature - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Tarek El-Ariss to Discuss War, Nature, and Water Politics at Biennale Arte 2026
articles.excerpt: Tarek El-Ariss will examine how crises alter perceptions of nature and reframe sustainability during a lecture at Biennale Arte 2026.
articles.content: Tarek El-Ariss is scheduled to speak at an event during Biennale Arte 2026 on November 21, 2026. Taking place at Teatro Piccolo Arsenale from 16:00 to 17:30, the lecture will be introduced and moderated by Rasha Salti. The session addresses how crises and wars not only damage the environment but also unsettle perceptions of nature. Drawing from everyday scenes such as saving water jars for bathing during wartime in Lebanon, the discussion traces longer histories and mythologies of water and greenery from the Garden of Eden to Greek and Islamic traditions, while focusing on the oasis as a recurring fantasy. The lecture posits that environmental practices do not necessarily emerge from ethical choices, often arising instead through habit, fear, or the quest for survival. Sustainability is reframed as a negotiation that interrogates the politics of purity and control to imagine alternative futures. Admission to the event is free until venue capacity is reached.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | LERATO SHADI | Unfolding - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Lerato Shadi's Performance Unfolding To Be Presented At Biennale Arte 2026
articles.excerpt: Lerato Shadi's performance titled Unfolding, focusing on memory and collective processes, will meet audiences on November 21, 2026, within Biennale Arte 2026.
articles.content: Shaped around memory, visibility, and collective processes, Unfolding is structured as a performance examining how meaning is produced and transmitted through bodies. The event will take place on November 21, 2026, from 12:00 to 12:40 in the Sala d’Armi E space. The work unfolds through a group relay structure where participants move to the stage, wrap a stone with red wool, and pass the transformed object to another participant. Through this repeated action, the object gradually changes form, accumulating time, touch, and traces of multiple hands. While wrapping becomes a gesture of protection and connection, passing the stone evokes histories and knowledge carried collectively rather than individually. Featuring Camille Badirou, Trovania Dellile, Viviana Medina, Rebecca Pokua Korang, and the artist herself, attendance requires a valid Biennale Arte 2026 admission ticket.

articles.originalTitle: FRIEDA EKOTTO | Resilience Against Value: Authored Practices of Repair in Otobong Nkanga and Ibrahim Mahama - La Biennale di Venezia

articles.title: Loro Piana Celebrates Cashmere Fineness at New York Exhibition
articles.excerpt: The Loro Piana Cashmere Award event and exhibition in New York celebrate cashmere fiber with a fineness of 12.89 microns and Inner Mongolian herders.
articles.content: Held at The Brant Foundation in New York, the 2025 Loro Piana Cashmere of the Year Award celebrated fiber measuring 12.89 microns in fineness. The event also unveiled the Master of Cashmere exhibition, highlighting the Italian house's history and manufacturing expertise. Established in 2015, the award has contributed to improving cashmere fineness. Chief executive officer Frédéric Arnault emphasized that cashmere sits at the heart of the brand's identity. The eleventh edition honored three pairs of cashmere herders from Inner Mongolia. The first prize went to greasy cashmere weighing 135.8 kg with a diameter of 12.89 microns. A micron equals one-thousandth of a millimeter, while human hair measures 70 microns. Winners receive a financial reward per kilo and a silver comb. Deputy chairman Pier Luigi Loro Piana noted his journey in China began in the 1980s, building strong relationships with local communities. Additionally, the company launched the Resilient Threads project last year to protect steppes and biodiversity in Sukhbaatar Province. The program partners with the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification, the Sustainable Fiber Alliance, and the Odyssey Conservation Trust. In September, a new knitwear complex opened in Italy's Piedmont region.

articles.originalTitle: Claude Monet | Waterlilies | L1406 - The National Gallery, London
articles.title: Claude Monet's 1905 Waterlilies Painting on Display in London
articles.excerpt: Claude Monet's 1905 painting Waterlilies forms part of his series inspired by his water gardens in Giverny. The artwork is housed at the National Gallery in London.
articles.content: After renting a house in Giverny west of Paris in 1883, Claude Monet eventually purchased the property and transformed the grounds into water gardens. Once the gardens matured, Monet turned to depicting them, making the water garden the subject of more than two hundred pictures. Between 1905 and 1908, he painted over sixty views of the pond exploring the contrast between tangible flowers and lily pads and the reflections of the unseen sky and overhanging trees. Housed at the National Gallery in London, Waterlilies exemplifies this series. In the painting, white flowers closest to the viewer feature purple accents for depth, while receding flowers are rendered in simple touches of white, yellow, pink, and red. The water itself consists of myriad tones of violets, blues, turquoise, and greens. The painting was included in Monet's 1909 exhibition at Durand-Ruel's gallery in Paris. Measuring 87 by 100 cm, the oil on canvas work is part of the Kenneth C. Griffin Collection.

articles.originalTitle: About the Punk to Pop exhibition - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: V&A Museum Exhibition Explores Cultural Transformation from Punk to Pop
articles.excerpt: V&A South Kensington prepares to launch a comprehensive exhibition examining the explosion of music, art, and fashion between 1972 and 1985 in March 2027.
articles.content: Opening on 13 March 2027 at V&A South Kensington, the Punk to Pop exhibition re-examines the creative explosion across music, art, and fashion from 1972 to 1985. Spanning three acts and approximately 300 objects, the showcase traces a historical trajectory starting from glam rock and disco, moving through underground subcultures like punk, Goth, and New Romantics, and concluding with digital-era pop culture. Featuring prominent acts such as Sex Pistols, Grace Jones, Blondie, Joy Division, and Wham!, the exhibition demonstrates how self-determined artists responded to political turbulence and austerity. Highlighted items include album artwork by Jamie Reid, handwritten lyrics by Ian Curtis, Mick Jones's first guitar, and photographs by Andy Warhol. Through theatrical staging, fashion, and stage costumes, the multi-sensory presentation celebrates how music provided a platform for individuality, sexuality, and cultural experimentation during a transformative era.
